Subject: RFI: Compartmentalization evidence and incident scenarios

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. As part of our vendor review we need a concise packet that demonstrates how Redwood compartments customer workloads, the controls that prevent cross-tenant access, and a short set of realistic incident scenarios (how Redwood detects, isolates, and recovers). CloudBank needs both architecture artifacts (network/partition diagrams) and operational playbooks for auditors.

Could you provide: 1) a topology/compartment diagram 2) short narrative (2–3 pages) of typical attack scenarios and mitigations 3) artifacts you can share (logs/evidence) that show isolation enforcement?

We are on a tight timeline — can you get something to us by EOD next Friday (Jun 20)? If you can include a contact for a technical walkthrough that would help.

Thanks,
Alan

Mateo — attaching the first-pass topology. Highlights:
- Logical compartments are enforced at three layers: network fencing (VPC/subnet isolation), runtime tenant-id enforcement in the inference fabric, and kv-cache tagging that prevents cross-tenant cache reuse.
- Control plane is separated into a customer-managed control-plane proxy for Private deployments; hosted customers have a multi-tenant control plane with strict RBAC and telemetry.
- Egress paths: default deny; explicit egress rules per tenant.

Notes for packet: I recommend we include a short appendix that explains how kernel selection and model variants are scoped to a tenant-bound runtime to reduce the chance of model-state leakage.

Attachment: compartment-diagram-v2.png (PNG, 1.2MB) — diagram shows zones: Customer Enclave, Inference Fabric, Control Plane (separate), Operator Plane (restricted), and Bastionless Egress Gateways.

Kimberly Park
Principal Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: compartment-diagram-v2.png]
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Compartmentalization evidence and incident scenarios

Kimberly — good diagram. I added a short threat-model summary and three incident scenarios you can drop into the narrative:

1) Stale KV-cache contamination: detection via cache-access anomaly; remediation via cache invalidation + tenant-scoped cache flush; post-incident evidence: cache eviction logs + request traces.
2) Control-plane credential compromise: detection via abnormal rollout activity; remediation via immediate rollback and key rotation; post-incident evidence: control-plane audit logs + signed attestations of rotation.
3) Sidecar network egress misconfiguration leading to lateral reachability: detection through egress policy violation alerts + netflow sampling; remediation via emergency policy application and zone quarantine; post-incident evidence: netflow captures + applied policy snapshot.

I’ll draft a 2-page threat-model summary and a sample operator checklist for each scenario. We should sanitize all logs in the evidence packet and include timestamps/IDs so CloudBank auditors can follow a signal chain without exposure.

Irene Choi
Staff Security Architect | Redwood Inference

Alan — attached is the consolidated packet as requested. Summary of contents below and quick notes on evidence provenance.

Attachment list (included):
- compartment-diagram-v2.png (diagram of logical and network compartments)
- evidence-packet.zip (sanitized logs + telemetry + audit snapshots)
- operational-playbook.pdf (incident checklists and operator steps)

Executive summary (short):
- Multi-layer compartmentalization: network-level segmentation (VPC/subnet/ACL), runtime tenant enforcement, and storage/kv tagging.
- Detection & isolation: telemetry-backed anomaly detection on KV/cache access patterns, control-plane audit feed correlation, and egress policy monitors.
- Recovery & forensics: deterministic rollback paths for model rollouts, key rotation playbooks, and signed audit traces for post-incident validation.

Evidence provenance: the logs in evidence-packet.zip are sanitized extracts from a dedicated test tenant and internal service telemetry; timestamps and request IDs are included for traceability.

We’ve also uploaded a read-only folder with the same artifacts here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1cloudbank-evidence
